title: CoServe: Efficient Collaboration-of-Experts (CoE) Model Inference with Limited Memory
problem: Collaboration-of-Experts (CoE) inference on memory-constrained edge devices (e.g., RTX 3080Ti with 12 GB GPU memory) requires serving hundreds of expert models (e.g., 300+ ResNet101/YOLOv5 experts totaling 60 GB) that cannot fit in GPU memory, forcing expert swapping from CPU or SSD where switching latency accounts for over 90% of total inference latency.
motivation: CoE systems achieve higher accuracy than single large models (99.9% vs. 92% for circuit board defect detection) and must run at the edge for privacy and latency reasons, but the memory-constrained expert-switching bottleneck makes existing MoE-style management strategies (LRU, FCFS) severely inefficient for CoE's deterministic routing structure.
method: CoServe takes advantage of a key property of Collaboration-of-Experts systems: they pre-determine which experts each request needs before execution, making expert requirements predictable—unlike Mixture-of-Experts systems where routing is decided at runtime. It uses three strategies to leverage this predictability: grouping requests that use the same expert to keep it loaded in GPU memory longer, removing experts that won't be needed for upcoming requests when GPU memory fills up (starting with the largest ones to free space quickly, then removing rarely-used ones), and using hardware benchmarks beforehand to find the optimal GPU memory allocation and CPU-GPU computation split.
key_novelty: CoServe's core idea is exploiting the fact that Collaboration-of-Experts systems determine expert requirements before execution, enabling intelligent request scheduling and expert eviction strategies that Mixture-of-Experts systems cannot achieve since their routing is only determined at runtime.
contributions: Identification of expert dependency as the key overlooked property enabling efficient CoE serving, distinct from MoE
Dependency-aware request scheduling (grouping by expert, load-balancing across CPU+GPU executors) reducing expert switches by up to 93.87%
Dependency-aware expert management with two-stage offline-probability-guided eviction policy
4.5x to 12x throughput improvement over Samba-CoE on real intelligent manufacturing workloads

metrics.speedup: 4.5x to 12x throughput over Samba-CoE on NUMA and UMA devices
metrics.other: expert switching reduced by up to 93.87% (1060 to 65 switches); expert switching latency is 90%+ of total inference latency in baseline

limitations: Evaluation uses only circuit board inspection workloads with ResNet101/YOLOv5 experts; generalization to language-model CoE or highly dynamic routing distributions is not demonstrated.
primary_theme: Dependency-aware scheduling and memory management for CoE model serving
